samples.summary: Making `readOnly` a mount-effect dep in notes-view creates a new YorkieNoteStore per role downgrade, but that store's constructor `doc.subscribe(...)` is never released (no `dispose()`, and notes-view's cleanup only disposes the editor)
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143` subscribes in the constructor and stores no unsubscribe handle; the class has no `dispose()`. The new cleanup at `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:150-155` calls only `editor.dispose()` and nulls `storeRef`, unlike the docs path which the same PR fixed by adding `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` and calling it (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:574`). Slides already has the same fix (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:376`, called at `slides-view.tsx:1216`). Effect: every `editor → viewer` downgrade leaves one permanently-subscribed store (its handler only snapshots a selection onto the dead store, so the effect is a leak rather than a stray write). The fix belongs on `yorkie-note-store.ts` + `notes-view.tsx`.

samples.summary: A throwaway `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` is discarded without calling the newly added `dispose()`, leaving the constructor's `doc.subscribe` attached for the document's lifetime
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:224` — `new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(content.document);`. The store is never retained or disposed, so the subscription installed at `yorkie-doc-store.ts:669` stays live on a document that outlives it. The new `dispose()` doc comment (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:679-687`) states it must be called "whenever the store is discarded while its document remains attached" — this is the one other construction site in the repo and it does not comply.

samples.summary: After `dispose()`, `getStore().setPageSetup(badGeometry)` still throws from `assertUsablePageSetup` instead of being a silent no-op, contradicting the "a disposed handle stays usable for reads and silently ignores writes" contract the rest of the revocation follows
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3293-3308` — `guardedSetPageSetup` returns early only for `readOnly`; it runs `assertUsablePageSetup(setup)` (which throws, see `editor.ts:1023-1033`) before delegating to the now-dead `revocableStore.setPageSetup`. The stale holder this whole change is aimed at (e.g. the page-setup dialog, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:125`, which already documents that this path throws) therefore gets an exception from a disposed handle where every other mutator is a no-op. Fix belongs on the new code: check the revoked state before validating.

samples.summary: Switching share-link resolution to a polling `useQuery` makes a *background* refetch failure tear down an open shared session for every shared surface, because the render gate treats `error` as fatal even when cached `resolved` data is still present
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:1125` — `if (!token || error || !resolved)` renders "Link unavailable". With `refetchInterval: 60_000` and `retry: 1`, react-query keeps `data` but also sets `error` after a failed background refetch, so a transient API/network failure replaces the live editor for all five consumers routed through this component (`SharedDocsLayout` :371, `SharedNotesLayout` :418, `SharedBoardLayout` :447, `SharedSlidesLayout` :552, `SharedDocumentLayout` :292). Previously the resolve ran once and a later failure could not evict the view. Gate on `error && !resolved` if the intent is only to close genuinely revoked links.

samples.summary: Design docs and a code comment still describe `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`, a field this change replaced with `undoFloorMark` / `undoFloorDepth` / `undoFloorIdentityUsable`
samples.evidence: `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:323` ("Reference impls: `docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` (Docs, with `undoFloor`)"), `docs/design/notes/notes.md:399` ("mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`"), `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:345` and `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:125` ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`"), and `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:49` ("reads its `undoFloor` *after* the write lands") all name a field that no longer exists. The three sibling stores also still use the depth-only floor the change proved wrong for a capped stack; nothing in CI checks nested design docs.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` now serialises the whole document twice per batch, and typing/Enter/paste in TextEditor now open a batch per keystroke — a per-keystroke cost added to every MemDocStore-backed host
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts` batch entry now does `cloneDocument(this.doc)` plus `JSON.stringify(beforeClone)` up front (in addition to the existing exit-time clone+stringify), while `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1019` wraps every `handleInput` in `withUndoUnit` → `doc.batch`. The MemDocStore consumers are `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:431` (every slides text box), `packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:503` and `packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/docs-scenarios.tsx:108`. Small for text boxes, but the docs demo/harness mount whole documents through the same store.

samples.summary: `sharing.md` still describes the share link as resolved once when the page opens; the new periodic revalidation, its interval, and the fact that a sustained resolve failure now closes an open session are undocumented
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sharing.md:35` ("Anonymous user opens /shared/:token → Frontend resolves token via API") and the surrounding flow describe a load-time resolve. The change introduces `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:88`) plus refetch-on-focus and view eviction on error, and makes `role` a live value that three view mount effects now key on — none of which is recorded in the design doc that owns this contract (nested design docs are not link-checked by CI either).
searchedFor: grep 'fixed for the lifetime|role is fixed|resolved once'

finding.summary: An in-flight `EditorAPI.paste()` bypasses the new dispose-time revocation: the clipboard-read continuation writes through `textEditor.pasteContent()`, which has no `disposed` check
finding.evidence: `api.paste` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3974-4006) awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()` and then calls `textEditor.pasteContent({html,text})` at editor.ts:3997 (and :4005). `neuterMutations(api)` in `dispose()` only replaces the *entry point* on the api object — a paste that already started resumes on the captured `textEditor` local, so the neuter never sees it. `TextEditor.pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1668) checks `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting` but NOT `this.disposed`, and `runPaste` (text-editor.ts:1588-1601) executes `job()` synchronously for any payload below `LARGE_PASTE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD` — only the deferred large-paste branch consults `this.disposed` (text-editor.ts:1609). `Cmd+Shift+V`'s resumed read *does* guard (text-editor.ts:4261 `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;`), which shows the guard was intended here too. Reachable from the docs context menu Paste item (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:272) on a `/shared/:token` session that is downgraded editor→viewer while the clipboard permission prompt is up — exactly the scenario the diff's dispose comment (editor.ts:4433-4442) says it revokes. Fix belongs on `pasteContent`: add the `this.disposed` early return.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `TextEditor.pasteContent` checks `readOnly` and `pasting` but NOT `disposed`. That is not the code in this repository: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1671` is `if (this.disposed) return;`, sitting ahead of the readOnly check (1673), the pasting check (1677) and the write path `pasteFromParts` (1679). The guard is armed on the disposal path the finding describes — `EditorAPI.dispose()` calls `textEditor?.dispose()` (editor.ts:4486) and `TextEditor.dispose()` sets `this.disposed = true` as its first statement (text-editor.ts:6081), synchronously, so an in-flight `api.paste()` resuming from `await navigator.clipboard.read()` and calling `textEditor.pasteContent(...)` (editor.ts:4018, 4026) returns without writing. The dispose comment at editor.ts:4470-4474 explicitly names this route as one of the three revoked, pointing at `this.disposed` in text-editor.ts. A regression test for exactly the claimed scenario (dispose while the clipboard read is pending) exists and asserts no write: packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:1093-1104, with the pending-clipboard stub at 1071-1087 and a live-editor control at 1106. The reviewer's ancillary claims about runPaste (1596) and deferPaste (1609) are accurate but unreachable for a disposed editor because pasteContent already returned. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: `dispose()` revokes only the api's own mutators; `getStore()` / `getDoc()` still hand out live writable handles after disposal, and a holder keeps them across the editor's lifetime
finding.evidence: `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` and `getDoc: () => doc` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3317-3318) have no `disposed` check. The comment at editor.ts:4485-4495 argues the two accessors are covered *for read-only* because they are backed by `readOnlyDocStore` — that coverage does not exist for disposal, which is baked-in `readOnly`'s replacement in this delta. A concrete holder: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68` constructs `new FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), () => editor.getStore().snapshot())` and keeps it in a ref; `FindReplaceState.replaceActive`/`replaceAll` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:57-87) write straight through that captured `Doc`, so a replace issued against a disposed editor still lands a CRDT write that `neuterMutations` cannot see. Same shape for `packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386`. Fix belongs on the new code: gate the accessors (or swap in the read-only store) on `disposed`.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `getDoc()`/`getStore()` hand out live writable handles after `dispose()` because neither accessor has a `disposed` check. Verified against the repo: the handles are guarded upstream of the accessors, not in them. `editor.ts:1138-1140` wraps the store at construction with `revocableDocStore(docStore, () => disposed)` and builds the returned `Doc` over it (`new Doc(readStore)`); `getStore()` returns `pageSetupGuardedStore`, a proxy whose target is that same `revocableStore` (editor.ts:3309-3319), and its one special-cased member routes through `revocableStore.setPageSetup` (editor.ts:3307). `dispose()` sets `disposed = true` at editor.ts:4475. `revocableDocStore` (store/read-only.ts:190-228) then serves every member from `readOnlyDocStore`, which no-ops any member not in the reader allowlist (read-only.ts:21-30, 96-117). The concrete holder cited is therefore covered: `FindReplaceState.replaceMatch` calls `this.doc.deleteText/insertText` (find-replace.ts:78-87), and `Doc` delegates at call time to `this.store.deleteText/insertText` (model/document.ts:288-306) — the revocable proxy — so a replace against a disposed editor performs no CRDT write, and the `snapshot()` callback in docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68 is likewise a no-op rather than a throw. The second cited site, bridge.ts:386, is `getStore().canUndo()`, a read in the allowlist. The claimed evidence lines are also mislocated (accessors are at editor.ts:3338-3339).
